questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What does political science study?

options.A: Only the government and its laws
options.B: The state, government, political institutions, power, authority, political behaviour, public policy, political ideas and relations among political actors
options.C: Only elections and voting behaviour
options.D: Only international relations and diplomacy

questions.explanation: Political science studies the state, government, political institutions, power, authority, political behaviour, public policy, political ideas and relations among political actors.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is the difference between political science and politics?

options.A: Political science is the study of government; politics is the study of society
options.B: Political science is the systematic study of political life; politics refers to the activities and processes through which power, authority and collective decisions are contested and exercised
options.C: Political science is theoretical; politics is practical
options.D: There is no difference between them

questions.explanation: Political science is the systematic study of political life; politics refers to the activities and processes through which power, authority and collective decisions are contested and exercised.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Why is the Constitution important in Indian political science?

options.A: It establishes the organs of government, distributes powers, limits public authority, guarantees rights and provides the framework for representative government
options.B: It only lists the fundamental duties of citizens
options.C: It only provides for the election of the President
options.D: It only establishes the judiciary

questions.explanation: The Constitution establishes the organs of government, distributes powers, limits public authority, guarantees rights and provides the framework for representative government.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is a state in political science?

options.A: A politically organised community of people living in a defined territory under an organised government and possessing sovereignty
options.B: A group of people sharing a common culture
options.C: An international organisation
options.D: A political party

questions.explanation: A state is a politically organised community of people living in a defined territory under an organised government and possessing sovereignty.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What are the four essential elements of a state?

options.A: Population, territory, government and sovereignty
options.B: Population, constitution, government and army
options.C: Territory, flag, anthem and government
options.D: Government, judiciary, legislature and executive

questions.explanation: The four essential elements of a state are population, territory, government and sovereignty.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Why is population an essential element of a state?

options.A: A state requires people who form its permanent human community; there is no universally fixed minimum population for statehood
options.B: A state requires a minimum of one million people
options.C: A state requires people only for voting purposes
options.D: Population is not an essential element of a state

questions.explanation: A state requires people who form its permanent human community; there is no universally fixed minimum population for statehood.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Why is territory an essential element of a state?

options.A: A state exercises public authority over a defined geographical area, including land and the relevant territorial jurisdiction
options.B: A state must have a minimum of 1000 square kilometres of land
options.C: Territory is only important for defence purposes
options.D: Territory is not an essential element of a state

questions.explanation: A state exercises public authority over a defined geographical area, including land and the relevant territorial jurisdiction.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Why is government an essential element of a state?

options.A: Government provides institutions and authorities through which the state makes, implements and interprets laws
options.B: Government is only needed to collect taxes
options.C: Government is only needed during elections
options.D: Government is not an essential element of a state

questions.explanation: Government provides institutions and authorities through which the state makes, implements and interprets laws.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is sovereignty?

options.A: The supreme authority of a state within its territory and its independence from external control in its sovereign affairs
options.B: The power of the government to make laws only
options.C: The power of the judiciary to interpret laws
options.D: The power of the people to elect their representatives

questions.explanation: Sovereignty is the supreme authority of a state within its territory and its independence from external control in its sovereign affairs.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is internal sovereignty?

options.A: The state's supreme authority over persons and institutions within its territory
options.B: The independence of a state from other states
options.C: The power of the state to declare war
options.D: The power of the state to make treaties

questions.explanation: Internal sovereignty is the state's supreme authority over persons and institutions within its territory.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is external sovereignty?

options.A: The independence of a state from the authority of other states, subject to international law and obligations it accepts
options.B: The state's supreme authority over persons within its territory
options.C: The power of the state to regulate foreign trade
options.D: The power of the state to maintain diplomatic relations

questions.explanation: External sovereignty is the independence of a state from the authority of other states, subject to international law and obligations it accepts.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Who is associated with the classical theory of sovereignty?

options.A: Jean Bodin
options.B: Karl Marx
options.C: John Locke
options.D: Montesquieu

questions.explanation: Jean Bodin is a major early theorist of sovereignty; later theorists such as Thomas Hobbes also developed influential accounts.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is popular sovereignty?

options.A: The principle that ultimate political authority rests with the people
options.B: The principle that the monarch has ultimate authority
options.C: The principle that the judiciary has ultimate authority
options.D: The principle that the legislature has ultimate authority

questions.explanation: Popular sovereignty is the principle that ultimate political authority rests with the people.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is the difference between state and government?

options.A: The state is the enduring political community with territory and sovereignty; government is the set of institutions and office-holders that administer the state and may change after elections
options.B: The state changes after elections; government is permanent
options.C: There is no difference between state and government
options.D: The state is a temporary institution; government is permanent

questions.explanation: The state is the enduring political community with territory and sovereignty; government is the set of institutions and office-holders that administer the state and may change after elections.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is the difference between state and nation?

options.A: A state is a political-legal organisation with territory, government and sovereignty; a nation is a community connected by a shared identity, history, culture or sense of belonging
options.B: A state is a cultural community; a nation is a political organisation
options.C: There is no difference between state and nation
options.D: A state is always smaller than a nation

questions.explanation: A state is a political-legal organisation with territory, government and sovereignty; a nation is a community connected by a shared identity, history, culture or sense of belonging.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is a nation-state?

options.A: A political state whose population is understood, to a significant degree, as forming a nation; in practice, many states contain multiple national, linguistic or cultural communities
options.B: A state with only one political party
options.C: A state with no constitution
options.D: A state that is part of a larger empire

questions.explanation: A nation-state is a political state whose population is understood, to a significant degree, as forming a nation; in practice, many states contain multiple national, linguistic or cultural communities.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is a multinational state?

options.A: A state that contains more than one national or culturally distinct community within one sovereign state
options.B: A state that is part of the United Nations
options.C: A state with multiple governments
options.D: A state with multiple constitutions

questions.explanation: A multinational state contains more than one national or culturally distinct community within one sovereign state.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is a unitary state?

options.A: A unitary state has a constitutionally centralised system in which the central authority holds ultimate legal authority, though it may delegate powers to local or regional bodies
options.B: A state with a federal division of powers
options.C: A state with no central government
options.D: A state that is part of a confederation

questions.explanation: A unitary state has a constitutionally centralised system in which the central authority holds ultimate legal authority, though it may delegate powers to local or regional bodies.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is a federal state?

options.A: A federal state constitutionally divides governmental powers between a national government and constituent regional governments, with each exercising authority in its assigned sphere
options.B: A state with a single central government
options.C: A state with no written constitution
options.D: A state with a hereditary monarch

questions.explanation: A federal state constitutionally divides governmental powers between a national government and constituent regional governments, with each exercising authority in its assigned sphere.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is a confederation?

options.A: A confederation is a union of sovereign or substantially autonomous political units that delegate limited powers to a common body, usually under an agreement
options.B: A state with a strong central government
options.C: A state with a single constitution
options.D: A state with no regional governments

questions.explanation: A confederation is a union of sovereign or substantially autonomous political units that delegate limited powers to a common body, usually under an agreement.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is a welfare state?

options.A: A welfare state accepts responsibility for promoting social and economic well-being through public services, social protection and measures addressing inequality
options.B: A state that provides only defence services
options.C: A state that does not intervene in the economy
options.D: A state that provides only law and order

questions.explanation: A welfare state accepts responsibility for promoting social and economic well-being through public services, social protection and measures addressing inequality.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is a secular state?

options.A: A secular state does not establish an official religion as the basis of state authority and protects freedom of conscience and religion according to its constitutional framework
options.B: A state that bans all religions
options.C: A state that promotes one official religion
options.D: A state that has no constitution

questions.explanation: A secular state does not establish an official religion as the basis of state authority and protects freedom of conscience and religion according to its constitutional framework.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is a sovereign republic?

options.A: A sovereign republic is an independent state in which the head of state is not a hereditary monarch and public authority is exercised under a constitutional or legal order
options.B: A state with a hereditary monarch
options.C: A state that is part of a confederation
options.D: A state with no constitution

questions.explanation: A sovereign republic is an independent state in which the head of state is not a hereditary monarch and public authority is exercised under a constitutional or legal order.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is government?

options.A: Government is the system of institutions and persons authorised to make, implement and interpret public decisions and laws
options.B: Government is the same as the state
options.C: Government is only the legislature
options.D: Government is only the judiciary

questions.explanation: Government is the system of institutions and persons authorised to make, implement and interpret public decisions and laws.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What are the three principal organs of government?

options.A: The legislature, executive and judiciary
options.B: The parliament, president and prime minister
options.C: The army, police and judiciary
options.D: The central government, state government and local government

questions.explanation: The three principal organs of government are the legislature, executive and judiciary.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is the legislature?

options.A: The legislature is the law-making organ of government; it also debates public issues, represents citizens, approves taxation and expenditure, and holds the executive accountable
options.B: The legislature implements laws and policies
options.C: The legislature interprets laws and resolves disputes
options.D: The legislature is the same as the executive

questions.explanation: The legislature is the law-making organ of government; it also debates public issues, represents citizens, approves taxation and expenditure, and holds the executive accountable.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is the executive?

options.A: The executive implements laws and policies and administers the day-to-day functions of government
options.B: The executive makes laws
options.C: The executive interprets laws
options.D: The executive is the same as the legislature

questions.explanation: The executive implements laws and policies and administers the day-to-day functions of government.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is the judiciary?

options.A: The judiciary interprets laws, resolves disputes and protects constitutional and legal rights through courts
options.B: The judiciary makes laws
options.C: The judiciary implements laws
options.D: The judiciary is the same as the executive

questions.explanation: The judiciary interprets laws, resolves disputes and protects constitutional and legal rights through courts.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is separation of powers?

options.A: Separation of powers is the principle of distributing legislative, executive and judicial functions among different organs to prevent concentration of authority
options.B: Separation of powers is the principle that all powers should be concentrated in one organ
options.C: Separation of powers is the principle that the judiciary should control the legislature
options.D: Separation of powers is the principle that the executive should control the judiciary

questions.explanation: Separation of powers is the principle of distributing legislative, executive and judicial functions among different organs to prevent concentration of authority.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What are checks and balances?

options.A: Checks and balances are constitutional mechanisms through which each branch or institution can restrain or review certain actions of other branches
options.B: Checks and balances are financial rules for government expenditure
options.C: Checks and balances are rules for election funding
options.D: Checks and balances are procedures for constitutional amendments

questions.explanation: Checks and balances are constitutional mechanisms through which each branch or institution can restrain or review certain actions of other branches.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is a parliamentary form of government?

options.A: A parliamentary system is one in which the executive is drawn from and remains politically responsible to the legislature, especially the elected lower house
options.B: A system in which the executive is completely separate from the legislature
options.C: A system in which the monarch has absolute power
options.D: A system in which the judiciary controls the executive

questions.explanation: A parliamentary system is one in which the executive is drawn from and remains politically responsible to the legislature, especially the elected lower house.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is a presidential form of government?

options.A: A presidential system has a separately elected or constitutionally independent executive president who ordinarily serves a fixed term and is not dependent on legislative confidence to remain in office
options.B: A system in which the president is a ceremonial head
options.C: A system in which the executive is responsible to the legislature
options.D: A system in which the monarch is the executive head

questions.explanation: A presidential system has a separately elected or constitutionally independent executive president who ordinarily serves a fixed term and is not dependent on legislative confidence to remain in office.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is a semi-presidential system?

options.A: A semi-presidential system combines a directly elected president with a prime minister and cabinet that are generally responsible to the legislature
options.B: A system in which the president is the only executive authority
options.C: A system in which the prime minister is the only executive authority
options.D: A system in which the judiciary appoints the executive

questions.explanation: A semi-presidential system combines a directly elected president with a prime minister and cabinet that are generally responsible to the legislature.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is a coalition government?

options.A: A coalition government is formed when two or more political parties agree to govern together, usually because no single party has a legislative majority
options.B: A government formed by a single party with a clear majority
options.C: A government formed by the military
options.D: A government formed by the judiciary

questions.explanation: A coalition government is formed when two or more political parties agree to govern together, usually because no single party has a legislative majority.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is a minority government?

options.A: A minority government is an administration that does not command an absolute majority of seats on its own but remains in office through support, confidence arrangements or legislative cooperation
options.B: A government formed by a single party with a clear majority
options.C: A government formed by the military
options.D: A government that has been defeated in an election

questions.explanation: A minority government is an administration that does not command an absolute majority of seats on its own but remains in office through support, confidence arrangements or legislative cooperation.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is a caretaker government?

options.A: A caretaker government is a temporary administration that manages routine government functions during a transition, subject to applicable constitutional conventions and legal limits
options.B: A government that has full powers to make new policies
options.C: A government formed by the military
options.D: A government that is elected for a fixed term

questions.explanation: A caretaker government is a temporary administration that manages routine government functions during a transition, subject to applicable constitutional conventions and legal limits.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is a constitutional government?

options.A: A constitutional government exercises public power under and within the limits of a constitution
options.B: A government that has no constitution
options.C: A government that is not limited by any law
options.D: A government formed by the military

questions.explanation: A constitutional government exercises public power under and within the limits of a constitution.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is an authoritarian government?

options.A: An authoritarian government concentrates political power and restricts meaningful political competition, accountability or civil liberties
options.B: A government that is limited by a constitution
options.C: A government that respects all civil liberties
options.D: A government formed by a coalition of parties

questions.explanation: An authoritarian government concentrates political power and restricts meaningful political competition, accountability or civil liberties.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is a totalitarian system?

options.A: A totalitarian system seeks extensive state or ruling-party control over political, social and often private life, usually through an official ideology and coercive institutions
options.B: A system with limited government power
options.C: A system with a ceremonial monarch
options.D: A system with a strong judiciary

questions.explanation: A totalitarian system seeks extensive state or ruling-party control over political, social and often private life, usually through an official ideology and coercive institutions.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is a monarchy?

options.A: A monarchy is a system in which the head of state is a monarch, commonly holding office by hereditary succession
options.B: A system in which the head of state is elected
options.C: A system in which the head of state is appointed by the judiciary
options.D: A system in which there is no head of state

questions.explanation: A monarchy is a system in which the head of state is a monarch, commonly holding office by hereditary succession.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is an absolute monarchy?

options.A: An absolute monarchy is a system in which the monarch exercises extensive governing authority with few effective constitutional restraints
options.B: A system in which the monarch's powers are limited by a constitution
options.C: A system in which the monarch is a ceremonial head
options.D: A system in which the monarch is elected

questions.explanation: An absolute monarchy is a system in which the monarch exercises extensive governing authority with few effective constitutional restraints.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is a constitutional monarchy?

options.A: A constitutional monarchy is a system in which the monarch's powers are limited by a constitution and elected institutions
options.B: A system in which the monarch has absolute power
options.C: A system in which there is no monarch
options.D: A system in which the monarch is elected

questions.explanation: A constitutional monarchy is a system in which the monarch's powers are limited by a constitution and elected institutions.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Who developed the influential sociological analysis of bureaucracy as a rational-legal organisation?

options.A: Max Weber
options.B: Karl Marx
options.C: John Locke
options.D: Montesquieu

questions.explanation: Max Weber developed the influential sociological analysis of bureaucracy as a rational-legal organisation.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is democracy?

options.A: Democracy is a system of government in which political authority is ultimately derived from the people, exercised directly or through representatives chosen in genuine elections
options.B: Democracy is a system in which the monarch has absolute power
options.C: Democracy is a system in which the military rules
options.D: Democracy is a system in which only the wealthy can vote

questions.explanation: Democracy is a system of government in which political authority is ultimately derived from the people, exercised directly or through representatives chosen in genuine elections.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is the literal meaning of democracy?

options.A: Democracy comes from the Greek words demos (people) and kratos (rule or power), commonly translated as rule by the people
options.B: Democracy means rule by the king
options.C: Democracy means rule by the rich
options.D: Democracy means rule by the military

questions.explanation: Democracy comes from the Greek words demos (people) and kratos (rule or power), commonly translated as rule by the people.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Who is associated with the phrase 'government of the people, by the people, for the people'?

options.A: Abraham Lincoln
options.B: George Washington
options.C: Thomas Jefferson
options.D: John Locke

questions.explanation: Abraham Lincoln is associated with the phrase, in his Gettysburg Address of 1863.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is direct democracy?

options.A: Direct democracy allows citizens to participate directly in making public decisions rather than acting only through elected representatives
options.B: Direct democracy is a system in which citizens elect representatives to make decisions
options.C: Direct democracy is a system in which the monarch makes all decisions
options.D: Direct democracy is a system in which the judiciary makes all decisions

questions.explanation: Direct democracy allows citizens to participate directly in making public decisions rather than acting only through elected representatives.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is representative democracy?

options.A: Representative democracy is a system in which citizens elect representatives to make public decisions and govern on their behalf
options.B: Representative democracy is a system in which citizens make all decisions directly
options.C: Representative democracy is a system in which the monarch makes all decisions
options.D: Representative democracy is a system in which the judiciary makes all decisions

questions.explanation: Representative democracy is a system in which citizens elect representatives to make public decisions and govern on their behalf.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is liberal democracy?

options.A: Liberal democracy combines electoral democracy with constitutional limits, civil liberties, political pluralism, rule of law and protections for individual rights
options.B: Liberal democracy is a system in which the government controls all aspects of life
options.C: Liberal democracy is a system in which only the wealthy can vote
options.D: Liberal democracy is a system in which the military rules

questions.explanation: Liberal democracy combines electoral democracy with constitutional limits, civil liberties, political pluralism, rule of law and protections for individual rights.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is participatory democracy?

options.A: Participatory democracy emphasises broad and continuing citizen involvement in decision-making beyond periodic elections
options.B: Participatory democracy emphasises only periodic elections
options.C: Participatory democracy emphasises rule by the military
options.D: Participatory democracy emphasises rule by the judiciary

questions.explanation: Participatory democracy emphasises broad and continuing citizen involvement in decision-making beyond periodic elections.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is deliberative democracy?

options.A: Deliberative democracy emphasises informed public discussion, reason-giving and consideration of different viewpoints in collective decision-making
options.B: Deliberative democracy emphasises voting without discussion
options.C: Deliberative democracy emphasises rule by the military
options.D: Deliberative democracy emphasises rule by the judiciary

questions.explanation: Deliberative democracy emphasises informed public discussion, reason-giving and consideration of different viewpoints in collective decision-making.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What are the essential features of democracy?

options.A: Popular sovereignty, free and fair periodic elections, universal adult franchise, political equality, rule of law, civil liberties, political pluralism, accountability and peaceful transfer of power
options.B: Only free and fair elections
options.C: Only universal adult franchise
options.D: Only rule of law

questions.explanation: The essential features of democracy include popular sovereignty, free and fair periodic elections, universal adult franchise, political equality, rule of law, civil liberties, political pluralism, accountability and peaceful transfer of power.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is universal adult franchise?

options.A: Universal adult franchise is the principle that adult citizens have the right to vote without discrimination on grounds such as wealth, sex, caste or religion, subject to lawful qualifications
options.B: Universal adult franchise is the principle that only property owners can vote
options.C: Universal adult franchise is the principle that only men can vote
options.D: Universal adult franchise is the principle that only educated people can vote

questions.explanation: Universal adult franchise is the principle that adult citizens have the right to vote without discrimination on grounds such as wealth, sex, caste or religion, subject to lawful qualifications.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is political equality?

options.A: Political equality means that citizens have equal political status and equal basic political rights, including the principle of one person, one vote and equal value of each vote
options.B: Political equality means that all citizens have equal wealth
options.C: Political equality means that all citizens have equal education
options.D: Political equality means that all citizens have equal social status

questions.explanation: Political equality means that citizens have equal political status and equal basic political rights, including the principle of one person, one vote and equal value of each vote.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is majority rule?

options.A: Majority rule is a decision-making principle under which the option receiving more than the competing alternatives is accepted, subject to constitutional rights and protections for minorities
options.B: Majority rule means that the majority can violate minority rights
options.C: Majority rule means that only the majority community can vote
options.D: Majority rule means that the military makes all decisions

questions.explanation: Majority rule is a decision-making principle under which the option receiving more than the competing alternatives is accepted, subject to constitutional rights and protections for minorities.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Why are minority rights important in a democracy?

options.A: They protect individuals and groups from exclusion or oppression and ensure that majority decisions remain within constitutional and human-rights limits
options.B: They allow the majority to rule without any limits
options.C: They allow the military to intervene in politics
options.D: They allow the judiciary to make all decisions

questions.explanation: Minority rights protect individuals and groups from exclusion or oppression and ensure that majority decisions remain within constitutional and human-rights limits.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is rule of law?

options.A: Rule of law means that everyone, including public authorities, is subject to law, and that law is applied through fair, public and accountable procedures
options.B: Rule of law means that the king is above the law
options.C: Rule of law means that the military is above the law
options.D: Rule of law means that the judiciary is above the law

questions.explanation: Rule of law means that everyone, including public authorities, is subject to law, and that law is applied through fair, public and accountable procedures.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is political pluralism?

options.A: Political pluralism recognises and permits the coexistence and competition of diverse political parties, interests, beliefs and organisations
options.B: Political pluralism means that only one political party is allowed
options.C: Political pluralism means that the military controls politics
options.D: Political pluralism means that the judiciary controls politics

questions.explanation: Political pluralism recognises and permits the coexistence and competition of diverse political parties, interests, beliefs and organisations.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is the difference between democracy and dictatorship?

options.A: Democracy provides meaningful popular participation, political competition and accountability; dictatorship concentrates power in one ruler or a small group and restricts political competition
options.B: Democracy concentrates power in one ruler; dictatorship provides popular participation
options.C: There is no difference between democracy and dictatorship
options.D: Democracy is rule by the military; dictatorship is rule by the people

questions.explanation: Democracy provides meaningful popular participation, political competition and accountability; dictatorship concentrates power in one ruler or a small group and restricts political competition.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is the difference between direct and representative democracy?

options.A: Direct democracy involves citizens deciding public questions themselves; representative democracy involves citizens electing representatives to decide and govern
options.B: Direct democracy involves elected representatives; representative democracy involves citizens deciding directly
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: Direct democracy is rule by the military; representative democracy is rule by the judiciary

questions.explanation: Direct democracy involves citizens deciding public questions themselves; representative democracy involves citizens electing representatives to decide and govern.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is the basic structure doctrine in India?

options.A: It is the constitutional principle that Parliament's power to amend the Constitution under Article 368 cannot be used to destroy its basic structure
options.B: It is the principle that Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution without limits
options.C: It is the principle that the judiciary can amend the Constitution
options.D: It is the principle that the President can amend the Constitution

questions.explanation: The basic structure doctrine is the constitutional principle that Parliament's power to amend the Constitution under Article 368 cannot be used to destroy its basic structure.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which Supreme Court case is associated with the basic structure doctrine?

options.A: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
options.B: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978)
options.C: Golaknath v. State of Punjab (1967)
options.D: Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980)

questions.explanation: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) is associated with the basic structure doctrine.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Is democracy part of the basic structure of the Indian Constitution?

options.A: Yes. The Supreme Court has recognised democracy as part of the Constitution's basic structure
options.B: No. Democracy is not part of the basic structure
options.C: Only the Preamble mentions democracy
options.D: Democracy can be removed by a simple majority

questions.explanation: Yes. The Supreme Court has recognised democracy as part of the Constitution's basic structure.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is the constitutional voting age in India?

options.A: 18 years
options.B: 21 years
options.C: 16 years
options.D: 25 years

questions.explanation: The voting age for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies is 18 years, following the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What is a political institution?

options.A: A political institution is an established structure or set of rules through which political authority is organised, exercised, limited and made accountable
options.B: A political institution is a political party
options.C: A political institution is an election
options.D: A political institution is a pressure group

questions.explanation: A political institution is an established structure or set of rules through which political authority is organised, exercised, limited and made accountable.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: What are the major political institutions in India?

options.A: The Union executive, Parliament, state executive, state legislatures, judiciary, Election Commission, Comptroller and Auditor General, Finance Commission and local self-government institutions
options.B: Only Parliament and the judiciary
options.C: Only the Election Commission and the Finance Commission
options.D: Only the Union executive and state executives
