options.D: Article 326

questions.explanation: Article 356 provides for provisions in case of failure of constitutional machinery in States.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which article provides for the power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and the procedure therefor?

options.A: Article 368
options.B: Article 356
options.C: Article 352
options.D: Article 326

questions.explanation: Article 368 provides for the power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and the procedure therefor.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an essential element of a state?

options.A: A written constitution
options.B: Population
options.C: Territory
options.D: Sovereignty

questions.explanation: A written constitution is not an essential element of a state. The four essential elements are population, territory, government and sovereignty.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a unitary state is correct?

options.A: The central authority holds ultimate legal authority, though it may delegate powers to local or regional bodies
options.B: Powers are constitutionally divided between national and regional governments
options.C: The constituent units are sovereign
options.D: There is no central government

questions.explanation: In a unitary state, the central authority holds ultimate legal authority, though it may delegate powers to local or regional bodies.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a federal state is correct?

options.A: Governmental powers are constitutionally divided between a national government and constituent regional governments, with each exercising authority in its assigned sphere
options.B: The central authority holds ultimate legal authority and may delegate powers
options.C: The constituent units are not constitutionally recognised
options.D: There is only one level of government

questions.explanation: In a federal state, governmental powers are constitutionally divided between a national government and constituent regional governments, with each exercising authority in its assigned sphere.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of a parliamentary form of government?

options.A: The executive is drawn from and remains politically responsible to the legislature
options.B: The executive has a fixed tenure and is not dependent on legislative confidence
options.C: The president is the sole executive authority
options.D: The judiciary appoints the executive

questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system, the executive is drawn from and remains politically responsible to the legislature, especially the elected lower house.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of a presidential form of government?

options.A: A separately elected or constitutionally independent executive president who ordinarily serves a fixed term and is not dependent on legislative confidence to remain in office
options.B: The executive is drawn from and remains politically responsible to the legislature
options.C: The prime minister is the sole executive authority
options.D: The judiciary appoints the executive

questions.explanation: In a presidential system, there is a separately elected or constitutionally independent executive president who ordinarily serves a fixed term and is not dependent on legislative confidence to remain in office.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of democracy?

options.A: Concentration of power in one ruler or a small group
options.B: Free and fair periodic elections
options.C: Universal adult franchise
options.D: Rule of law

questions.explanation: Concentration of power in one ruler or a small group is a feature of dictatorship, not democracy.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Rajya Sabha is correct?

options.A: It is a permanent House; approximately one-third of its members retire every two years
options.B: It is dissolved every five years
options.C: It is dissolved every six years
options.D: All its members retire at once every two years

questions.explanation: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House; it is not subject to dissolution, and approximately one-third of its members retire every two years.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a Money Bill is correct?

options.A: The Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend a Money Bill; it may make recommendations, and must return it within 14 days
options.B: The Rajya Sabha can reject a Money Bill
options.C: The Rajya Sabha can amend a Money Bill
options.D: The Rajya Sabha can delay a Money Bill indefinitely

questions.explanation: The Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend a Money Bill; it may make recommendations, and must return it within 14 days.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the First-Past-the-Post system is correct?

options.A: The candidate who receives more votes than any other candidate in a constituency wins, even without securing an absolute majority
options.B: The candidate who receives an absolute majority wins
options.C: Seats are allocated in proportion to votes received
options.D: The candidate is elected by the legislature

questions.explanation: Under FPTP, the candidate who receives more votes than any other candidate in a constituency wins, even without securing an absolute majority.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about India's federal structure is correct?

options.A: India has a federal constitutional structure with a strong Union and several unitary features; the Supreme Court has described the Constitution's federal character as part of its basic structure
options.B: India is a purely unitary state with no federal features
options.C: India is a confederation of sovereign states
options.D: India has no division of legislative powers

questions.explanation: India has a federal constitutional structure with a strong Union and several unitary features; the Supreme Court has described the Constitution's federal character as part of its basic structure.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Eleventh Schedule is correct?

options.A: It lists 29 subjects related to Panchayats
options.B: It lists 18 subjects related to Municipalities
options.C: It lists anti-defection provisions
options.D: It lists legislative subjects for the Union and States

questions.explanation: The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects related to Panchayats.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Twelfth Schedule is correct?

options.A: It lists 18 subjects related to Municipalities
options.B: It lists 29 subjects related to Panchayats
options.C: It lists anti-defection provisions
options.D: It lists legislative subjects for the Union and States

questions.explanation: The Twelfth Schedule lists 18 subjects related to Municipalities.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Article 254 is correct?

options.A: Under Article 254, the Parliamentary law generally prevails to the extent of repugnancy on a Concurrent List subject, subject to the constitutional exception where a State law reserved for and receiving Presidential assent may prevail in that State; Parliament can later override it
options.B: Under Article 254, the State law always prevails
options.C: Under Article 254, both laws are automatically void
options.D: Under Article 254, the Supreme Court decides which law prevails in each case

questions.explanation: Under Article 254, the Parliamentary law generally prevails to the extent of repugnancy on a Concurrent List subject, subject to the constitutional exception where a State law reserved for and receiving Presidential assent may prevail in that State; Parliament can later override it.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the election of the President of India is correct?

options.A: The President is elected indirectly by an electoral college consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States and the specified Union Territories of Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir, according to constitutional provisions
options.B: The President is elected directly by the people
options.C: The President is appointed by the Prime Minister
options.D: The President is elected by the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: The President is elected indirectly by an electoral college consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States and the specified Union Territories of Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir, according to constitutional provisions.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.topic: Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.chapter: Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the election of the Vice-President is correct?

options.A: By members of both Houses of Parliament, assembled at a joint meeting for this purpose, using proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and secret ballot; nominated members may vote
options.B: By the members of the Lok Sabha only
options.C: By the members of the Rajya Sabha only
options.D: By the people directly

questions.explanation: The Vice-President is elected by members of both Houses of Parliament, assembled at a joint meeting for this purpose, using proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and secret ballot; nominated members may vote.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Election Commission of India is correct?

options.A: It is an independent constitutional authority under Article 324
options.B: It is a statutory body under the Representation of the People Act
options.C: It is an executive body under the Ministry of Law
options.D: It is a judicial body under the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: The Election Commission of India is an independent constitutional authority under Article 324.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Model Code of Conduct is correct?

options.A: It is a set of guidelines issued by the Election Commission to regulate the conduct of political parties and candidates during elections; it is not itself a comprehensive statute
options.B: It is a constitutional amendment
options.C: It is a law passed by Parliament
options.D: It is a judicial order

questions.explanation: The Model Code of Conduct is a set of guidelines issued by the Election Commission to regulate the conduct of political parties and candidates during elections; it is not itself a comprehensive statute.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the anti-defection law is correct?

options.A: It provides grounds on which members of Parliament or State Legislatures may be disqualified for defection, under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution
options.B: It provides grounds for disqualification of the President
options.C: It provides grounds for disqualification of judges
options.D: It provides grounds for disqualification of civil servants

questions.explanation: Anti-defection law provides grounds on which members of Parliament or State Legislatures may be disqualified for defection, under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about pressure groups is correct?

options.A: A pressure group seeks to influence government decisions, laws or public policy without primarily seeking to form the government itself
options.B: A pressure group seeks to form the government
options.C: A pressure group is a constitutional body
options.D: A pressure group is a political party

questions.explanation: A pressure group is an organised group that seeks to influence government decisions, laws or public policy without primarily seeking to form the government itself.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about agenda-setting is correct?

options.A: Agenda-setting is the process by which media attention influences which issues people perceive as important, without necessarily determining what they think about those issues
options.B: Agenda-setting is the process by which the government sets its legislative agenda
options.C: Agenda-setting is the process by which the judiciary sets its case list
options.D: Agenda-setting is the process by which political parties select candidates

questions.explanation: Agenda-setting is the process by which media attention influences which issues people perceive as important, without necessarily determining what they think about those issues.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about devolution is correct?

options.A: Devolution is the transfer of meaningful powers, functions and resources to elected subnational governments that have a degree of autonomy
options.B: Devolution is the transfer of administrative responsibilities within the same level of government
options.C: Devolution is the concentration of authority at the central level
options.D: Devolution is the abolition of elected subnational governments

questions.explanation: Devolution is the transfer of meaningful powers, functions and resources to elected subnational governments that have a degree of autonomy.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about deconcentration is correct?

options.A: Deconcentration is the redistribution of administrative responsibilities within the same level of government, usually from central offices to field offices
options.B: Deconcentration is the transfer of authority from central to local governments
options.C: Deconcentration is the transfer of authority from local to central governments
options.D: Deconcentration is the abolition of field offices

questions.explanation: Deconcentration is the redistribution of administrative responsibilities within the same level of government, usually from central offices to field offices.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about delegation is correct?

options.A: Delegation is the transfer of specified decision-making or administrative functions to semi-autonomous bodies or agencies, while ultimate authority may remain with the delegating government
options.B: Delegation is the transfer of ultimate authority to local governments
options.C: Delegation is the concentration of authority at the central level
options.D: Delegation is the abolition of semi-autonomous bodies

questions.explanation: Delegation is the transfer of specified decision-making or administrative functions to semi-autonomous bodies or agencies, while ultimate authority may remain with the delegating government.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Gram Sabha is correct?

options.A: The Gram Sabha consists of all persons registered in the electoral rolls relating to a village within the area of a Gram Panchayat
options.B: The Gram Sabha consists of elected members of the Gram Panchayat
options.C: The Gram Sabha consists of officials appointed by the State Government
options.D: The Gram Sabha consists of members of the State Legislature

questions.explanation: The Gram Sabha consists of all persons registered in the electoral rolls relating to a village within the area of a Gram Panchayat.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Karnataka's rural local-government framework is correct?

options.B: It operates through Nagar Panchayats, Municipal Councils and Municipal Corporations
options.C: It operates through Ward Committees and District Planning Committees
options.D: It operates only through Gram Sabhas

questions.explanation: Karnataka's rural local-government framework operates through Gram Panchayats, Taluk Panchayats and Zilla Panchayats under the applicable Karnataka Panchayat Raj legislation.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a state from a government?

options.A: The state is the permanent sovereign political community; government is the set of institutions and office-holders that administer it
options.B: The state is the set of institutions; government is the permanent sovereign political community
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: The state changes after elections; government is permanent

questions.explanation: The state is the permanent sovereign political community; government is the set of institutions and office-holders that administer it.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes democracy from republic?

options.A: Democracy concerns popular participation and political accountability; a republic has a non-hereditary head of state. A country can be both democratic and republican
options.B: Democracy has a hereditary head of state; a republic concerns popular participation
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: A country can be either democratic or republican, but not both

questions.explanation: Democracy concerns popular participation and political accountability; a republic has a non-hereditary head of state. A country can be both democratic and republican.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes parliamentary government from presidential government?

options.A: In parliamentary government the executive is responsible to the legislature; in presidential government the executive has a separate constitutional mandate and fixed tenure
options.B: In parliamentary government the executive has a fixed tenure; in presidential government the executive is responsible to the legislature
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: In parliamentary government the head of state is always a monarch; in presidential government the head of state is always elected

questions.explanation: In parliamentary government the executive is responsible to the legislature; in presidential government the executive has a separate constitutional mandate and fixed tenure.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the legislature from the executive?

options.A: The legislature makes laws and scrutinises government; the executive implements laws and administers policy
options.B: The legislature implements laws; the executive makes laws
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: The legislature is always more powerful than the executive

questions.explanation: The legislature makes laws and scrutinises government; the executive implements laws and administers policy.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a political party from a pressure group?

options.A: A political party seeks governmental power through elections; a pressure group seeks to influence government policy
options.B: A political party seeks to influence government policy; a pressure group seeks governmental power through elections
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: A political party is a constitutional body; a pressure group is a statutory body

questions.explanation: A political party seeks governmental power through elections; a pressure group seeks to influence government policy.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes FPTP from proportional representation?

options.A: FPTP awards a constituency seat to the candidate with the most votes; proportional representation aims to translate vote shares into seats more proportionately
options.B: FPTP translates vote shares into seats proportionately; proportional representation awards a constituency seat to the candidate with the most votes
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: FPTP is used only for Rajya Sabha elections; proportional representation is used only for Lok Sabha elections

questions.explanation: FPTP awards a constituency seat to the candidate with the most votes; proportional representation aims to translate vote shares into seats more proportionately.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes governance from government?

options.A: Government is the formal machinery of the state; governance is the wider process of public decision-making and implementation involving state and non-state actors
options.B: Government is the wider process of decision-making; governance is the formal machinery of the state
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: Government involves only non-state actors; governance involves only state actors

questions.explanation: Government is the formal machinery of the state; governance is the wider process of public decision-making and implementation involving state and non-state actors.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes cooperative federalism from competitive federalism?

options.A: Cooperative federalism emphasises collaboration between levels of government; competitive federalism emphasises competition among governments to improve performance or attract resources
options.B: Cooperative federalism emphasises competition among governments; competitive federalism emphasises collaboration between levels of government
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: Cooperative federalism is a unitary system; competitive federalism is a confederation

questions.explanation: Cooperative federalism emphasises collaboration between levels of government; competitive federalism emphasises competition among governments to improve performance or attract resources.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes decentralisation from devolution?

options.A: Decentralisation is the broad distribution of authority downward; devolution is a stronger form involving transfer of powers and resources to elected lower-level governments
options.B: Decentralisation is a stronger form involving transfer of powers; devolution is the broad distribution of authority downward
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: Decentralisation is a unitary system; devolution is a federal system

questions.explanation: Decentralisation is the broad distribution of authority downward; devolution is a stronger form involving transfer of powers and resources to elected lower-level governments.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the basic structure doctrine is correct?

options.A: It is the constitutional principle that Parliament's power to amend the Constitution under Article 368 cannot be used to destroy its basic structure
options.B: It is the principle that Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution without limits
options.C: It is the principle that the judiciary can amend the Constitution
options.D: It is the principle that the President can amend the Constitution

questions.explanation: The basic structure doctrine is the constitutional principle that Parliament's power to amend the Constitution under Article 368 cannot be used to destroy its basic structure.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a joint sitting of Parliament is correct?

options.A: A joint sitting is a meeting of both Houses to resolve certain deadlocks over ordinary legislation under Article 108; it is not available for Money Bills or Constitutional Amendment Bills
options.B: A joint sitting is a meeting of both Houses to pass a Money Bill
options.C: A joint sitting is a meeting of both Houses to amend the Constitution
options.D: A joint sitting is a meeting of Parliament and the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: A joint sitting is a meeting of both Houses to resolve certain deadlocks over ordinary legislation under Article 108; it is not available for Money Bills or Constitutional Amendment Bills.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about judicial review is correct?

options.A: Judicial review is the power of courts to examine the constitutionality and legality of legislative and executive actions
options.B: Judicial review is the power of the legislature to review court decisions
options.C: Judicial review is the power of the executive to review court decisions
options.D: Judicial review is the power of the President to review court decisions

questions.explanation: Judicial review is the power of courts to examine the constitutionality and legality of legislative and executive actions.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Public Interest Litigation (PIL) is correct?

options.A: PIL is a form of litigation through which a person or organisation may approach a court to protect public interest or the rights of disadvantaged persons, subject to judicial rules
options.B: PIL is a form of litigation through which only the government can approach a court
options.C: PIL is a form of litigation through which only the President can approach a court
options.D: PIL is a form of litigation through which only the Prime Minister can approach a court

questions.explanation: PIL is a form of litigation through which a person or organisation may approach a court to protect public interest or the rights of disadvantaged persons, subject to judicial rules.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is correct?

options.A: The CAG audits receipts and expenditure of the Union and States and other bodies as provided by the Constitution and law
options.B: The CAG conducts elections
options.C: The CAG recommends the distribution of tax revenues
options.D: The CAG appoints judges

questions.explanation: The CAG audits receipts and expenditure of the Union and States and other bodies as provided by the Constitution and law.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Finance Commission is correct?

options.B: It audits government expenditure
options.C: It conducts elections
options.D: It appoints judges

questions.explanation: The Finance Commission recommends the distribution of certain tax revenues between the Union and States and among States, and principles for grants-in-aid and other matters referred to it under Article 280.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the registration of political parties in India is correct?

options.B: Registration of political parties is governed by Article 29A of the Constitution
options.C: Registration of political parties is governed by Article 324A of the Constitution
options.D: Registration of political parties is governed by Article 29 of the Constitution

questions.explanation: Article 324 provides the Election Commission's general constitutional authority; registration of political parties is specifically governed by Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about VVPAT is correct?

options.B: Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail is a system for online voting
options.C: Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail is a system for voter registration
options.D: Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail is a system for counting votes

questions.explanation: Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail is a system that allows voters to verify a printed paper slip corresponding to their vote, displayed for a brief period before it is deposited in a sealed box.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about corporatism is correct?

options.A: Corporatism is an arrangement in which organised interests, such as employer and worker associations, are formally incorporated into policy consultation or negotiation structures
options.B: Corporatism is an arrangement in which only political parties are consulted
options.C: Corporatism is an arrangement in which only the judiciary is consulted
options.D: Corporatism is an arrangement in which only the military is consulted

questions.explanation: Corporatism is an arrangement in which organised interests, such as employer and worker associations, are formally incorporated into policy consultation or negotiation structures.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about political socialisation is correct?

options.A: Political socialisation is the process through which individuals acquire political values, beliefs, attitudes and orientations
options.B: Political socialisation is the process through which political parties are registered
options.C: Political socialisation is the process through which elections are conducted
options.D: Political socialisation is the process through which laws are made

questions.explanation: Political socialisation is the process through which individuals acquire political values, beliefs, attitudes and orientations.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Right to Information Act, 2005 is correct?

options.A: It is an Indian law that gives citizens a statutory right to access information held by public authorities, subject to exemptions and procedures
options.B: It is an Indian law that gives citizens a statutory right to access information held by private companies
options.C: It is an Indian law that gives citizens a statutory right to access information held by foreign governments
options.D: It is an Indian law that gives citizens a statutory right to access information held by the judiciary only

questions.explanation: The Right to Information Act, 2005 is an Indian law that gives citizens a statutory right to access information held by public authorities, subject to exemptions and procedures.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Lokpal is correct?

options.A: The Lokpal is a statutory anti-corruption ombudsman at the Union level established under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013
options.B: The Lokpal is a constitutional court
options.C: The Lokpal is a political party
options.D: The Lokpal is an election commission

questions.explanation: The Lokpal is a statutory anti-corruption ombudsman at the Union level established under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a social audit is correct?

options.A: A social audit is a participatory process through which people examine public records and verify the implementation, expenditure and outcomes of public programmes
options.B: A social audit is a financial audit conducted by the CAG
options.C: A social audit is a judicial review of government actions
options.D: A social audit is an election audit conducted by the Election Commission

questions.explanation: A social audit is a participatory process through which people examine public records and verify the implementation, expenditure and outcomes of public programmes.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about sustainable governance is correct?

options.A: Sustainable governance integrates economic, social, institutional and environmental considerations into public decision-making for present and future generations
options.B: Sustainable governance focuses only on economic growth
options.C: Sustainable governance focuses only on environmental protection
options.D: Sustainable governance focuses only on social welfare

questions.explanation: Sustainable governance integrates economic, social, institutional and environmental considerations into public decision-making for present and future generations.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the GST Council is correct?

options.A: The GST Council is a constitutional body under Article 279A that makes recommendations on key aspects of the Goods and Services Tax
options.B: The GST Council is a statutory body under the Finance Act
options.C: The GST Council is a judicial body under the Supreme Court
options.D: The GST Council is an executive body under the Ministry of Finance

questions.explanation: The GST Council is a constitutional body under Article 279A that makes recommendations on key aspects of the Goods and Services Tax.
